title: Hosted API capacity follow-up: queue fanout mitigation, warm-pool prewarm, and fair-share admission plan
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary:
During the 2025-02-12 hosted API incident we observed cascading queue buildup in multiple GPU pools which triggered broad tenant throttles and long tail latencies. This ticket consolidates follow-ups from the incident retro, prioritizes fixes to avoid similar queue amplification, and sequences short-term mitigations and mid-term architectural changes.

Scope and goals:
- Implement a controlled fanout limiter to stop request duplication across hot shards.
- Add a warm-pool prewarm path to reduce cold-start amplification for bursty tenants.
- Introduce a fair-share admission modifier to prevent single-tenant storms from blocking others.
- Fix missing telemetry (queue depth per-tenant, admission-reject reasons) to improve runbook effectiveness.

Why unique: unlike prior tickets that focused on autoscaler hysteresis or eviction policies, this ticket bundles three complementary approaches (fanout control, targeted prewarm, admission fairness) that together reduce amplification and lower incident blast radius.

Root cause (brief):
- A micro-regression in the shard-routing layer caused some requests to be broadcast to multiple replicas under transient load, increasing effective concurrency by ~2-3x for affected tenants.
- Autoscaler priming lag and conservative soft-eviction thresholds allowed queues to grow while backpressure signals were delayed.
- Telemetry for per-tenant queue depth and admission-reject reasons was incomplete, delaying operator detection and mitigation.

Success metrics:
- Reduce worst-case queue amplification factor to <1.2x for all pools in synthetic replay.
- <1% of requests experience >3x latency increase under 95th percentile traffic compared to baseline.
- Ensure per-tenant reject reason instrumentation available in Console and shipped dashboards.

Related artifacts and links:
- Incident postmortem: https://drive.company.internal/postmortems/2025-02-12-gpu-capacity-exhaustion
- Initial regression PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1482
- Telemetry dashboard mockups: https://drive.company.internal/designs/telemetry-tenant-queue
comments: 2025-02-18 - Priya Shah: Captured action items from retro. Prioritize low-lift mitigations that can be rolled in the next runtime patch. Marcus assigned to coordinate engineering work and validate telemetry gaps.

2025-02-19 - Marcus Lee: Investigated routing log traces. Found repeated 'broadcast_to_shards' calls originating from the shard router when the health-check window tripped on a minority of replicas. Drafted a local patch to gate broadcast during high load.

2025-02-20 - Aisha Malik: Telemetry team confirms tenant queue depth metrics are missing for scaled-down pools; adding instrumentation to runtime admission path. Will instrument 'admission.reject_reason' tag and emit slow-path histograms. Estimate 3 points.

2025-02-21 - Marcus Lee: Implemented fanout limiter prototype (feature branch: eng/limit-fanout). Adds per-request fanout budget and a per-tenant token-bucket limiter. Running unit and integration tests; synthetic replay looks promising (amplification factor reduced from 2.9x to 1.15x locally).

2025-02-22 - Tomás Rivera: Design note: warm-pool prewarm should be conservative — only prewarm for tenants with high burstiness score and critical tier. Proposed policy: threshold 95th-run rate > 100 req/min AND burstiness score > 0.7 -> prewarm up to 2 warm backfills. See design doc: https://drive.company.internal/designs/warm-pool-policy

2025-02-23 - Priya Shah: Safety review: confirm rollout includes feature flag and canary. Security: no new keys or external endpoints. Request that telemetry board be updated before canary so SRE can observe per-tenant queue depths in real time.

2025-02-24 - Marcus Lee: Opened PRs: runtime PR #1498 (fanout limiter), autoscaler PR #322 (prewarm hook), telemetry PR #88 (admission.reject_reason metrics). Linking here. Plan: land telemetry PR first, then fanout limiter behind feature flag, then prewarm hook in a staged rollout.

2025-02-25 - QA: Running synthetic tenant storm test (script: load-tests/storm-replay) against staging with feature flag on. Observed 12% lower p95 latency and queue depth plateau rather than spike. Noted an edge-case where warm-pool prewarm overshot desired GPU allocation for multi-tenant pools — need cap enforcement.

2025-02-26 - Marcus Lee: Cap enforcement added (PR #1507). Also added a soft-fallback to drop prewarm when global GPU utilization > 85%. Preparing rollout checklist and runbook updates. Assigned to deploy to canary tomorrow.

2025-02-26 - Priya Shah: Approving canary rollout pending SRE sign-off. SRE owners: Aisha Malik, Jordan Kim. Update runbook to reflect new 'admission.reject_reason' categories and automated alert thresholds (queue_depth_per_tenant > 500 for 30s).

2025-02-26 - Jordan Kim: SRE sign-off granted. Will monitor canary for 24h and escalate on >5% error budget burn or sustained p95 latency regression. Set up dashboard and pager routing for early detection.
decision_summary: We agreed to ship a layered mitigation strategy: 1) telemetry fixes first so SRE can observe and validate, 2) fanout limiter behind a feature flag to immediately stop amplification, 3) targeted warm-pool prewarm for high-burst tenants with global caps, and 4) a fair-share admission modifier to weight tenant admission under pressure. All changes will be behind feature flags and rolled to canary before broader rollout.

Merge fanout limiter behind feature flag and run staged canary (owner: Marcus Lee, estimate: 5)
Add warm-pool prewarm cap to autoscaler and verify global utilization soft-bail (owner: Tomás Rivera, estimate: 5)
Implement fair-share admission modifier and add integration tests to replay harness (owner: Priya Shah, estimate: 8)
Update runbook and console dashboards with new reject_reason and per-tenant queue depth graphs (owner: Jordan Kim, estimate: 3)
Post-rollout retrospective and metrics review after 2 weeks on canary (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2025-03-12)
